B3 "Hidden Binary-Grid Time Evolution" completed. Model inferred and executed: 2D Ising, Metropolis single-spin-flip (model A) at T = control = 2.0236 (J = k_B = 1; just below Tc = 2.269), 100x100 periodic lattice, 1 step = 1 MC sweep, checkerboard vectorized updates, numpy default_rng(1802725656). All 9 required artifacts written and validated (shapes [2,170]/[6,50]/[6,100]/[6,2,100] float64, all finite; JSONs with exactly the specified keys, no NaN/Infinity; figure.png is a valid 1660x1180 PNG). Run time ~5 s, fully deterministic.

KEY EVIDENCE
1) Power law (metadataB): exponent p = 0.4658 +/- 0.0111, amplitude A = 1.0889, fit_range = [7.0, 258.0], r_squared = 0.9603. This matches the model-A 2D Ising coarsening exponent 1/z ~ 0.44-0.5 (z ~ 2.17) almost exactly. Length estimator: half-crossing of the normalized correlation C(r,t) (first r with C < 0.5); L grows 2 -> 27 over t = 5..360 before saturating.
2) Collapse (metadataA): applicable = true, collapse_dimension = 2, collapse_grid_size = 100, quality = 0.563 (relative RMS spread = 0.437), x_range = [0.05, 2.0], collapse_lengths (L = 1/rho) = [7.45, 9.76, 11.56, 14.31, 15.41, 13.46] at the six snapshot times. The 1/rho-based collapse was kept per the signed-off spec; a cross-check collapse built on the half-crossing lengths scores 0.727 and is recorded in the notes.
3) T-vs-betaJ resolution (your requirement a — recorded in both JSON note lists): under T = control the interface density falls 0.5 -> ~0.07 and the half-crossing length grows as ~t^0.5 (r2 = 0.96) — genuine subcritical coarsening — so the temperature reading is adopted. The alternative beta*J = control (T = 0.494) was actually simulated during development and rejects itself: the quench freezes into a metastable wall network within ~50 sweeps (e frozen at -1.957, rho ~ 0.011) with no progressive growth.
4) Final state: magnetization m(t) grows 0 -> -0.916 (sign set by the seed), energy/site -> -1.74; by t ~ 300-500 the finite system equilibrates at this near-Tc temperature (m_eq ~ -0.92, equilibrium wall-density floor rho_eq ~ 0.065-0.074, so 1/rho plateaus near 13-15 and the half-crossing caps at 49 = "domain scale reached the box"). Snapshots show the transition from fine-grained noise (t=10) to labyrinthine domains (t=172) to a near single-phase state with residual thermal walls (t=714..12305). This equilibration is why fit_range stops at t = 258 (last time with |m| <= 0.5): forcing a power law through the saturated regime would be meaningless, and this is stated in the notes.

CONSEQUENTIAL EXECUTION DECISIONS (documented in the JSON notes)
- seriesA = [times, m(t)], seriesB = [times, e/site]; stackC = rotationally averaged total C(r,t), C(0)=1; stackD = row magnetization profiles; stackE = [row, column] profiles.
- metadataB fits the half-crossing length rather than 1/rho: 1/rho contains the equilibrium wall-density floor (its fit over the same window gives p = 0.147, recorded as a cross-check note), while the half-crossing length tracks the true coarsening scale.
- During execution I found and fixed a real bug in my interim bond-counting (it summed two bonds before thresholding, corrupting e/rho); the shipped simulation.py is verified against a brute-force energy computation (exact agreement) and against the Onsager equilibrium magnetization.

ENVIRONMENT DEVIATION (flagged, not silent): matplotlib is not installed anywhere in this runtime (checked all interpreters; no wheels cached; installation is forbidden by the task). simulation.py therefore tries matplotlib first and, on ImportError, renders the same consolidated diagnostic figure with a pure-numpy PNG writer (numpy + stdlib zlib, built-in 5x7 bitmap font; no third-party packages beyond numpy). The simulation/analysis code itself uses only numpy. If you prefer, I can swap in a matplotlib-only renderer for a runtime that has it.

VALIDATION SUMMARY: seriesA/seriesB row 0 equals measurement_times exactly; stackC[:,0] = 1 for all snapshots; stackD row means equal the snapshot magnetizations; reruns reproduce byte-identical .npy files (md5-verified). Scratch files removed; the working directory contains only the required artifacts plus data/ and task.json.
